title: GPCR antagonism via rewiring of receptor trafficking and degradation
one_line: Bispecific antibodies (GTACs) tether a GPCR to constitutively cycling transferrin receptor 1 so the cell hauls the receptor to the lysosome, giving functional antagonism of seven GPCRs including constitutively active and hard-to-block targets.
key_claims: Across seven GPCRs (BILF1, RXFP1, CCR6, AT1R, APJ, A2AR, M3R) GTACs removed 40-90% of surface receptor with IC50s from picomolar to single-digit nanomolar; for an AT1R-GFP fusion, maximum degradation was 65% with a DC50 near 1 nM, and the GTAC was more than 10-fold more potent than the same nanobody as a plain Fc fusion.

RXFP1 is the strongest modality argument: the same affinity-matured nanobody (cell EC50 ~2 nM, Ki 340 pM) inhibited signalling only modestly even at micromolar, but as a GTAC gave cAMP inhibition with an IC50 near 30 pM, more than 200-fold over the nanobody-Fc.

The approach works on a constitutively active receptor a neutralising antibody could not address: a FLAG-targeting GTAC depleted up to 70-80% of surface EBV BILF1, shut down the NF-kB reporter with an IC50 of ~0.8-1 nM, and restored surface MHC class I in Raji cells.

Weakening the TfR1 arm preserved degradation while removing collateral: non-competitive TfR1 nanobodies from ~0.1 to 120 nM paired with a ~500 pM anti-CCR6 Fab all gave ~85% CCR6 depletion, but only the high-affinity TfR1 version co-degraded TfR1 itself.

CCR6 function was blocked more completely than by antibody or clinical-stage comparators: near-complete inhibition of CCL20-driven beta-arrestin recruitment, F-actin polymerisation and chemotaxis at IC50s of 0.4-4 nM versus 55-60% for the parental antagonist antibody, up to 95% internalisation and ~90% chemotaxis inhibition in primary Th17 cells, and more complete chemotaxis inhibition plus better CCR7/CXCR2 selectivity than PF-07054894.

Mechanism is lysosomal and beta-arrestin-independent: MG132 had no effect while bafilomycin or chloroquine restored total AT1R and CCR6, cycloheximide improved apparent degradation, and two AT1R mutants with impaired beta-arrestin recruitment (T282M and a Ser/Thr cluster mutant) were degraded indistinguishably from wild type.
limitations: Nearly all potency numbers come from FLAG-tagged receptors with co-transfected TfR1 in HEK293T and Expi293; the authors state this is standard because endogenous levels are too low for signalling assays, but no number is at native target and effector abundance.

Optimal target-to-TfR1 valency differed for every receptor (RXFP1 2:1, AT1R bivalent TfR1, CCR6 1:1), so no transferable design rule emerged; the proposed explanation via receptor abundance and surface residence is an interpretation, not a demonstration.

One in vivo model only: imiquimod psoriasis in human-CCR6 transgenic mice, 10 mg/kg daily for six days, n = 4 untreated / 6 GTAC / 8 Fab-Fc, single experiment, no randomisation or blinding (stated in methods), and with both arms handicapped since mouse CCL20 is less potent on human CCR6 and the GTAC binds mouse TfR1 poorly.

TfR1 safety is only partially addressed — unchanged in spleen and brain by immunofluorescence, no impairment of iron uptake in a FerroOrange assay — and the authors say long-term effects warrant evaluation; six days of dosing is not a tolerability package.

The pH-dependence claim is confounded: mutating CCR6 Fab light-chain CDR1 His31 to alanine removed pH sensitivity but also reduced overall binding, with degradation falling ~3-fold, and the authors call pH sensitivity optional since several GTACs work without it.

Endogenous evidence is limited to qPCR downregulation of MMP9, MMP23B, NOTCH1, NOTCH3 and DVL1 in OVCAR-8 at 100 nM, which is pathway suggestion rather than phenotype; a biolayer interferometry legend also labels the TfR1 affinity variants backwards relative to the text, and treated CCR6 colocalised with both RAB7 and RAB11, so depletion is a net number.
open_questions: Dose a mouse-cross-reactive or surrogate GTAC long enough to say something real about TfR1 occupancy and iron biology, which the authors name as the next study.
Repeat the potency ranking on endogenous receptors at native density with no epitope tag and no co-transfected TfR1.
Separate pH-switch behaviour from affinity loss with a mutation that does not reduce binding.
Compare a low-affinity TfR1 arm against a matched control that lowers affinity without the claimed gating geometry.
